comparison: Both affirm the cohort characterization (C1, C14-C19, C150-C151). OpenEval provides detailed validation of demographic and treatment data. Peer reviewers explicitly praised the cohort as 'impressive and nicely characterized' with appropriate analysis.

Both support PTMC/ACTA2 findings (C6, C58-C65). OpenEval validates the 'disconnected' pattern observation and developmental comparisons. Peer reviewers explicitly stated 'Changes in Sertoli and peritubular cells appear valid.'

OpenEval supports Leydig cell findings (C4-C5, C82-C89, C147) as well-documented with appropriate markers. Both support gene expression patterns P3 and P4 (C104-C107). OpenEval validates the GO associations and integration with histological data. Peer reviewers accepted these findings as part of the overall transcriptomic evidence.

Both support pattern P5 showing inflammation/fibrosis (C11, C13, C108-C112). OpenEval validates the extensive GO enrichment and correlation with histology. Peer reviewers accepted this as part of the 'convincing' evidence for rejuvenation and niche changes.

Both support the 'partial rejuvenation' conclusion (C10, C12, C113-C114, C143). OpenEval validates the integration of multi-modal evidence. Peer reviewers explicitly affirmed the 'signs of rejuvenation' were 'evidently demonstrated.'

Both rate the research surrogate application (C136, C149) as UNCERTAIN. OpenEval notes limited validation and concerns about tissue variability and inflammation. Peer reviewers similarly expressed concern about significant differences from adult cells and variability due to treatment regimens. Strong agreement on uncertainty.

OpenEval supports the mechanistic interpretations and broader literature context (C121-C135), validating the biological plausibility and appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific mechanistic claims.
